name: BookIt — Booking System
problem: Booking platforms break under concurrent reservations — double-bookings, failed payments without rollback, and silent notification failures erode user trust.
solution: A full-stack booking system with CQRS architecture that separates commands (CreateBooking, CancelBooking, RescheduleBooking) from queries, with real-time availability updates via WebSocket.
impact: CQRS with dedicated Command and Query handlers. Event-driven domain logic via EventBus. Real-time availability sync through Socket.IO gateway. 9 backend modules with shared type-safe packages.
outcomeMetric: 130 tests · CQRS architecture · 9 backend modules · Real-time WebSocket · CI/CD
demoNote: This is a sample project built to showcase code quality and architecture patterns. It runs in demo mode with simulated data. I value time — building more samples so you can evaluate my work across different domains. Clone the repo to explore the full codebase.

name: FlowBoard — Real-Time Collaborative Kanban
problem: Remote teams need real-time task visibility without page refreshes. Existing tools either lack real-time sync or require expensive per-seat licenses.
solution: A Kanban board with real-time WebSocket collaboration via Socket.IO + Redis pub-sub, fractional indexing for conflict-free drag-and-drop, 4-tier RBAC, AI-powered task parsing, and background job processing with Bull queue.
impact: 12+ NestJS modules forming a modular monolith. Real-time sync via Socket.IO with Redis adapter for multi-instance. AI task parsing via Claude API. Bull queue for email digests, audit logging, and overdue checks.
outcomeMetric: 202 tests · 12+ backend modules · Real-time WebSocket + Redis pub-sub · CI/CD · Fractional indexing

name: Money Management — Personal Finance App
problem: Personal finance tools are either too simple (spreadsheets) or too complex (enterprise accounting). No middle ground for individuals who want multi-account tracking with visual insights.
solution: A full-stack personal finance platform with a Laravel 13 API backend (Sanctum auth, Eloquent, PostgreSQL, Redis) and a Next.js 16 frontend. Multi-account management across 8 categories, transaction categorization, drag-and-drop organization, scheduled transactions, and exportable PDF/Excel reports.
impact: Full-stack with separate API repo. Unified financial view across 8 categories with real-time charts. PDF and Excel export for tax season. Sanctum token auth. Docker-containerized backend with PostgreSQL and Redis.
outcomeMetric: Laravel API + Next.js · PostgreSQL · Redis · Docker · 8 financial categories · PDF/Excel export
demoNote: Full-stack with separate repos — Frontend (GitHub link above) and Backend API: github.com/jeromejhipolito/money-management-api (Laravel 13, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker).

name: MerchantFlow — Cross-Border E-Commerce Ops
problem: Cross-border e-commerce teams juggle Shopify webhooks, multi-store order processing, shipment tracking, and inventory sync across fragmented tools — one missed webhook or failed fulfillment means lost revenue and angry customers.
solution: A modular monolith platform with Saga orchestration for order processing, transactional outbox for reliable event delivery, HMAC webhook verification, and BullMQ job queues — all with step-level idempotency and compensating transactions.
impact: 331 passing tests covering reliability patterns: webhook verification, deduplication, idempotency, saga compensation, outbox delivery, and state machine validation. Full jitter backoff prevents thundering herd on retries.
outcomeMetric: 331 tests · Saga orchestration · Transactional outbox · CI/CD · Modular monolith

name: AI Booking Agent
problem: A chatbot that books appointments will eventually book two people into one chair. The language model is the part that guesses, so anything it decides on its own is a guess — including whether you agreed to something.
solution: A salon booking agent where the model only reads the sentence. Every decision that must not be wrong lives below it: service names are matched against the real catalogue, slots come from a query, and a booking is authorised by a row the server wrote when the agent showed you a summary — not by a field the model emits. A database constraint makes overlapping appointments impossible under any race.
impact: 135 live assertions across three suites, each one firing a real workflow and then asking Postgres what actually happened. The whole suite runs against a deliberately weak self-hosted 7B model, which found six defects a sharper model would have hidden.
outcomeMetric: 135 live assertions · 14 workflows · 4 database constraints · 352 adversarial cases reviewed
codeDiff:
+ -- The guard the whole design rests on. Not a check in the code — a constraint,
+ -- so no code path, race or confused model can get past it.
+ CONSTRAINT appointment_no_double_booking
+   EXCLUDE USING gist (
+     stylist_id WITH =,
+     tstzrange(starts_at, ends_at) WITH &&
+   ) WHERE (status = 'confirmed')
+
+ -- tstzrange defaults to a half-open [) range, so a 10:00-10:45 and a 10:45-11:30
+ -- booking sit back to back without conflicting. No inventory lost to an off-by-one.
demoNote: No hosted demo: the agent runs on n8n against its own Postgres. The repository includes a one-command local stack and the three verification suites.
